title: 第十八章 描红
content_zh:
摸到了门道的边，江砚反倒栽了更大的跟头。

    那念头让他兴奋得几夜没睡好。一连几日，趁着秦伯出去看诊、庙里没人留意，他就躲到墙角，捡块炭、捡块砖，偷偷地试。

    他循着自己想通的那点理——挑自己真懂的、最简单的东西画。

    碗，他天天用，懂。

    可还是成不了。

    一连试了七八回，最好的一回，那碗口都收圆了，光也亮到了顶——偏偏到最后那一瞬，他心里“成了“两个字一冒头，喜得一激动，气就散了，光也跟着散了。

    每一次失败，都要呕一口血。

    不是大口的血，是一丝丝的腥，憋在喉咙里，咽下去，胃里翻江倒海。试到第三天，江砚整个人又垮了下去，脸白得没有一丝血色，走路都打飘。秦伯回来，瞧了他一眼，皱起眉，又给他抓了副补气血的药，嘴里嘟囔：“你这孩子，底子虚成这样，是怎么活到今天的。“

    江砚捧着那碗黑乎乎的药，心里又愧又急。

    愧的是，秦伯当他是大病初愈、底子亏，哪知道这血是他自己一笔一笔“画“出来的。急的是——他明明摸到了“懂“和“心“，怎么还是成不了？

    那天夜里，他又试。

    又败。又是一口血。

    江砚把炭头狠狠摔在地上，脊背抵着冰凉的庙墙，胸口剧烈起伏。

    他盯着砖上那一摊狼藉的乱墨，盯了很久很久。

    那墨痕，张牙舞爪，没一笔是稳的。起笔是急的，行笔是颤的，收笔是慌的。跟柴房那夜墙上的鬼画符，一个模样。

    跟……他从小到大写的字，一个模样。

    江砚忽然就想起了那个雨夜。

    魂穿之前，他趴在桌上赶检讨，写得一手鬼画符，老师拿着他的本子直摇头，说他“心不静，手太野，笔走得比脑子快“。

    心不静。手太野。

    笔走得比脑子快。

    江砚的呼吸，停了一拍。

    他低头，看着砖上这团乱墨。可不就是“手比脑子快“么。他心里明明想着一只稳稳当当的碗，可那炭头一落到砖上，就跟脱了缰似的，急吼吼地、潦草地、一笔不停地往下冲——他的“想“，根本没跟上他的“画“。

    念在前头，笔在后头，两下里脱了节。

    这画出来的，能是个什么东西？是个有形没魂、慌慌张张的残废碗。它“差一点“成，就败在这“一点“上——败在他这支笔，从来就稳不下来。

    江砚怔住了。

    他想起这本事的源头。它叫“鬼画符“。不是别的，正是他那一手谁也认不得、连自己都嫌乱的鬼画符。

    成也是它，败也是它。

    它给了他凭空造物的本事，可它本身那股“野“劲、那股“乱“劲，又让这本事死死地不可控。就像一匹烈马，能驮人千里，可你驾驭不住它，它就把你掀下来，踩死在地上。

    那……怎么才能驾驭？

    江砚的目光，慢慢从那团乱墨上，移开了。

    他想起一个东西。
content_en:
When he touched the edge of the doorway, Jiang Yan stumbled even more.

    That thought made him so excited that he couldn't sleep well for several nights. For several days, when Uncle Qin was out for medical treatment and no one in the temple was paying attention, he hid in the corner, picked up pieces of charcoal and bricks, and tried them secretly.

    He followed the logic he had figured out - choosing the simplest things to draw that he really understood.

    He uses bowls every day and understands them.

    But it still didn't work.

    He tried it seven or eight times in a row, and in the best one, the mouth of the bowl was rounded, and the light was shining to the top. But at the last moment, the word "became" appeared in his heart, and he was so happy and excited that his anger dissipated, and the light also dissipated.

    Every time he failed, he had to vomit blood.

    It wasn't a big mouthful of blood, but a trace of fishy smell, which was stuck in the throat. When I swallowed it, my stomach turned upside down. On the third day of the trial, Jiang Yan collapsed again. His face was so pale that he couldn't even walk without a trace of blood. Uncle Qin came back, glanced at him, frowned, and gave him some medicine to replenish qi and blood, muttering: "You kid, you are so weak, how did you survive to this day?"

    Jiang Yan held the bowl of dark medicine, feeling ashamed and anxious.

    What's embarrassing is that Uncle Qin thought he was just recovering from a serious illness and had a bad foundation. He didn't know that the blood was "painted" one by one by himself. The urgent thing is - he clearly has "understanding" and "heart", but why can't he succeed?

    That night, he tried again.

    Defeated again. Another mouthful of blood.

    Jiang Yan slammed the charcoal head to the ground, his back pressed against the cold temple wall, and his chest heaved violently.

    He stared at the messy ink on the bricks for a long, long time.

    The ink marks are like claws and teeth, and no stroke is safe. When you start writing, you are anxious, when you finish writing, you are trembling, and when you finish writing, you are panicked. It looks exactly like the ghostly drawings on the wall in the woodshed that night.

    It looks exactly like...the capital letters he used to write since childhood.

    Jiang Yan suddenly remembered that rainy night.

    Before his soul passed away, he was lying on the table to review, and he could write with ghostly marks. The teacher held his notebook and shook his head, saying that his "mind was not calm, his hands were too wild, and his pen moved faster than his brain."

    The heart is restless. Hands too wild.

    The pen moves faster than the brain.

    Jiang Yan's breathing paused for a beat.

    He lowered his head and looked at the mess of ink on the bricks. Isn't it just that "hands are faster than brains"? He was clearly thinking about a steady bowl, but as soon as the charcoal fell on the bricks, it seemed as if it was out of control, rushing down in a hurry, scribbling, and strokes - his "thinking" did not keep up with his "drawing".

    The reading is in the front, the writing is in the back, and the two are out of touch.

    What could this painting be? It is a shapeless, soulless, crippled bowl. It "almost" succeeded, but it failed on this "one point" - it failed because of his pen, which never stabilized it.

    Jiang Yan was stunned.

    He remembered the origin of this ability. It's called "Ghost Drawing Talisman". It's nothing else, it's the ghost-drawing talisman in his hand that no one can recognize, and even he finds it confusing.

    It is also the success, and it is also the failure.

    It gave him the ability to create things out of thin air, but its own "wild" energy and "chaotic" energy made this ability uncontrollable. It's like a fierce horse that can carry people thousands of miles, but if you can't control it, it will knock you off and trample you to the ground.

    So...how can I control it?

    Jiang Yan's eyes slowly moved away from the mess of ink.

    He remembered something.
